title: Self-Assembly of Gamma-Modified Peptide Nucleic Acids into Complex Nanostructures in Organic Solvent Mixtures
protocol: Download the DNA Design Toolbox into the folder with programming scripts.
Open a fourth-generation programming language compatible with the file extension “.m”.
Add the “DNAdesign” folder to the path using the command: addpath DNAdesign.
Run the script named “PNA3nanofiber.m” using the command: PNA3nanofiber.
Create variables called “thisSeqs” and “thisScore” by running the script.
Obtain multiple minimal scores by running the script repeatedly.
Manually confirm Watson-Crick complementarity of each domain for the specified SST structural motif.
Avoid using four consecutive C and G bases in sequences.
Select specific sequences for N-terminal functionalization with fluorescent dye and biotin molecules.
Include a minimum of 3 mini-PEG gamma-modifications on the backbone to enable pre-organized helical conformation.
Obtain γPNA component strands at 50 nmol scale synthesis with HPLC purification.
Resuspend each strand in deionized water to 300 µM concentrations.
Store resuspended strands in -20°C freezer until needed for experimentation.
Run a melt curve study for different combinations of complementary 2-oligomer and 3-oligomer subsets.
Use aqueous buffers such as 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) or preferred polar organic solvent like Dimethylformamide (DMF) or Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Aliquot 16.7 µL from the 300 µM stock of each oligomer.
Make final volume to 1000 µL in either PBS, DMSO, or DMF to obtain a 5 µM final concentration per strand.
Transfer the oligomer subset mixture to a 1 cm optical path quartz cuvette.
Perform variable temperature UV-Vis experiments in a spectrophotometer equipped with a programmable temperature block.
Collect data points for the melting curves over a temperature range of 15‒90 °C for both cooling and heating cycles at a rate of 0.5‒1 °C/min.
Keep samples for 10 min at 90 °C before cooling and at 15 °C before heating.
Determine the melting temperature (Tm) from the peak of the first derivative of the heating curve.
Verify that melting temperature ranges for 2-oligomer subsets are above 35 °C in all solvent cases.
Verify that corresponding 3-oligomer subsets show a considerable increase in Tm due to increased cooperativity.
Anneal samples for 22.5 h in a thermal cycler cooling from 90 to 20 °C.
Program the thermal cycler to hold at 90 °C for 5 min.
Ramp down from 90 to 70 °C at a constant rate of 0.1 °C/min.
Ramp down from 70 to 40 °C at a rate of 0.1 °C/3 min.
Ramp down from 40 to 20 °C at a rate of 0.1 °C/min.
Hold at 4 °C.
Store samples in 4 °C for 12‒24 h before characterization.
Prepare anneal batch samples in 75% DMSO: H2O (v/v) for micron-scale long 3-helix nanofibers.
Prepare anneal batch samples in 75% DMF: H2O (v/v) for micron-scale long 3-helix nanofibers.
Prepare anneal batch samples in 40% 1,4-Dioxane: H2O (v/v) for micron-scale long 3-helix nanofibers.
Aliquot 0.67 µL from the main stock to prepare 10 µL sub-stocks at 20 µM concentrations.
Make up the volume to 10 µl using deionized water for each oligomer sub-stock.
Aliquot 1 μL from the 20 µM sub-stocks for each oligomer and add it to a 200 µL PCR tube.
Add either 30 µL of anhydrous DMSO/DMF with 1 µL deionized water to make a final volume of 40 µL for the 75% DMSO and DMF cases, achieving a 500 nM oligomer concentration.
Add 16 µL of 1,4-Dioxane and adjust the total volume with deionized water to 40 µL for the 40% Dioxane solvent condition.
Prepare a humidity chamber from an empty pipette tips box by filling it with approximately 5 mL of water.
Prepare flow chamber using a microscope slide, two double-sided tape strips, and a nitrocellulose-coated coverslip.
Dip the coverslip in a beaker containing 0.1% collodion in amyl acetate to coat it with nitrocellulose and air-dry.
Make the nitrocellulose solution by diluting commercially available 2% collodion in amyl acetate with isoamyl acetate at a ratio of 20:1.
Weigh 1 mg of Biotin-BSA and dissolve it in 1 mL of 1x PBS.
Flow 15 μL of 1 mg/mL Biotin-BSA in 1x PBS buffer by placing the flow channel at an angle.
Incubate the flow channel for 2–4 min at room temperature in a humidified chamber.
Prepare the wash buffer by dissolving 1 mg of BSA in 1 mL of 1x PBS.
Wash the excess Biotin-BSA by flowing 15 μL of the wash buffer.
To passivate the surface, incubate the flow channel for 2–4 mins at room temperature in a humidified chamber.
Measure 0.5 mg of streptavidin and 1 mg of BSA and then dissolve using 1 mL of 1x PBS.
Flow 15 μL of 0.5 mg/mL streptavidin in 1x PBS containing 1 mg/mL BSA.
Incubate the flow channel for 2–4 min at room temperature in a humidified chamber.
Flow 15 μL of the wash buffer to wash away unbound Streptavidin.
Flow 15 μL of previously annealed batch of γPNA oligomers at 500 nM concentration per strand in either 75% DMSO, 75% DMF or 40% 1,4-Dioxane condition.
Incubate the flow channel for 2–4 mins at room temperature in a humidified chamber.
Prepare 1 mM Trolox in preferred solvent conditions by diluting 10-fold from a 10 mM stock of Trolox in DMSO (measure 2.5 mg of Trolox and dissolve in 1 mL of DMSO).
Wash the unbound nanostructures in the flow channel with 15 µL of 1 mM Trolox having the same solvent composition as the nanostructures.
Weigh 0.5 g of uranyl acetate in 50 mL of distilled water to prepare a 1% aqueous uranyl acetate stain solution.
Filter the 1% aqueous uranyl acetate stain solution using a 0.2 μm filter attached to a syringe.
Pipette 4 μl of sample onto the grid for 15 s.
Use a piece of filter paper to wick off the sample by bringing it in contact with the grid from the side.
Immediately add 4 μl of the stain solution onto the grid for 5 s.
Wick off the stain as before and hold the filter paper against the grid for 1-2 min to make sure the grid is dry.
Transfer the grid to a TEM specimen holder.
Image using a transmission electron microscope operated at 80 kV with magnification ranging from 10 K to 150K.
Obtain DNA oligomers of specified sequences from commercial oligonucleotide manufacturers synthesized at 25 nmol scale using standard desalting.
Resuspend these DNA sequences using RNase-free deionized water at 20 μM stock concentrations.
Aliquot 1 μL from the 20 µM sub-stocks for each γPNA or DNA oligomer and add it to a 200 µL PCR tube.
Add 30 µL of anhydrous DMSO and 1 µL of RNase-free deionized water to make the final volume to 40 µL.
Load the anneal batches on to the thermal cycler and anneal using the protocol mentioned in step 4.2.
Characterize γPNA-DNA hybrid nanostructures using the TIRF protocol following steps in section 5 or using TEM imaging protocol mentioned in section 6.
Prepare a 20% (wt/v) SDS main stock by measuring 20 mg of SDS and dissolving it in 100 µL of deionized water.
Prepare a 6% (wt/v) SDS sub-stock by aliquoting 3 µL from the 20% SDS stock and making the volume to 10 µL using deionized water.
Aliquot 1 μL from the 20 µM sub-stocks for each γPNA oligomer and add it to a 200 µL PCR tube.
Add 30 µL of anhydrous DMSO and 1 µL of 6% SDS to make the final volume to 40 µL to achieve SDS final concentration of 5.25 mM.
Add 30 µL of anhydrous DMSO and 1 µL of 20% SDS to make the final volume to 40 µL to achieve SDS final concentration of 17.5 mM.
Load anneal batches with varying SDS concentrations onto the thermal cycler.
Anneal samples using the protocol specified in step 4.2.
Characterize γPNA nanostructures in the presence of SDS using the TIRF protocol from section 5.
Alternatively, characterize γPNA nanostructures in the presence of SDS using the TEM imaging protocol from section 6.
